paper_metadata.title: A 32-Site 4-Channel Cochlear Electrode Array Pamela T. Bhatti, Sangwoo Lee and Kensall D. Wise

figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.caption: Figure 2.3.1: The 32-site 4-channel cochlear microsystem.

references.sentence: This paper presents a thin-film cochlear electrode array (Fig. 2.3.1) that achieves high site density and incorporates onboard circuitry for stimulus generation and position sensing.
A 14µm-thick boron-diffused silicon area forms the base of the array, which remains outside the cochlea to support circuitry for current generation, site selection, and position sensing (Fig. 2.3.1).
Realized in 0.5µm AMI CMOS, the 2.4mm × 2.4mm circuit chip (Fig. 2.3.2) is flip-chip bonded to the cochlear array via 45 gold lead tabs formed using the array process (Fig. 2.3.3).
Sixteen-bit command words (Fig. 2.3.4) are serially clocked in on the data line (DIN), latched, and validated in an error detection block (Fig. 2.3.5).
Each S/H output is buffered and applied to an analog current driver as shown in Fig. 2.3.6.
The S/H voltage is converted to a drive current (I) and mirrored to the output stage (5I) as a biphasic stimulus current ranging from 0 to ±500µA (Fig. 2.3.7).
